headline: Sépaq Daily Access Permits and Sector Check-ins
reservation: Entry requires a daily access pass purchased through the Sépaq website, which can sell out during peak fall foliage and summer weekends. This permit is separate from campsite or hut bookings, which typically open months in advance. Visitors should verify which of the three sectors—Pimbina, Diable, or L'Assomption—they are entering as they are not all internally connected by paved roads.

days.title: Rivers and Cascades of the Diable Sector

stops.name: Chute-du-Diable
stops.detail: Walk the curated trail to view the powerful falls, a staple of the park's central hydrography.

stops.name: Lac Monroe
stops.detail: Rent a canoe or kayak at the Centre de découverte to explore the glacial valley from the water.

days.driving: Allow 45–60 minutes; conditions vary by park entrance traffic.
days.note: The Diable sector is the most popular; aim for early entry to secure trailhead space.

days.title: Vertical Views and Highland Peaks
days.start: Suggested: 8:30 AM from the Lac Monroe Service Centre

stops.name: La Roche Lookout
stops.detail: Ascend through the maple forest for a sweeping view of the Vache Noire mountains and the river valley.

stops.name: La Corniche
stops.detail: Continue to this adjacent viewpoint for a different perspective over Lac Monroe and the southern peaks.

days.driving: Minimal driving once in the sector; shuttle bus use may be required seasonally.
days.note: Trails involve significant elevation; pace yourself according to local humidity levels.

days.title: Eastern Wilderness of Pimbina

stops.name: Chute-aux-Rats
stops.detail: Visit this 17-meter high waterfall located near the Pimbina gateway, often quieter than the Diable sector.

stops.name: Lac Provost
stops.detail: Enjoy the sandy beach area and the transition between the Laurentian shield and boreal forest.

days.driving: Allow 30–40 minutes from Saint-Donat; gravel sections possible.
days.note: This sector is geographically distinct; ensure your vehicle is fueled in Saint-Donat.

intel.title: Sector Disconnectivity
intel.text: The park is divided into sectors like Diable and Pimbina that are not linked by internal paved highways. Always check which gate matches your planned trailhead to avoid long detours around park boundaries.

intel.title: Trailhead Capacity
intel.text: Parking lots at La Roche and Chute-du-Diable frequently reach capacity by mid-morning on weekends. Sépaq staff may redirect traffic once lots are full; consider mid-week visits for easier access.

intel.title: Gateway Supplies
intel.text: Fuel and groceries are best secured in the town of Mont-Tremblant or Saint-Donat before entering park gates. There are no service stations located within the national park boundaries.

intel.title: Seasonal Road Closures
intel.text: Secondary gravel roads within the park may remain closed until late May due to thaw conditions. Winter access is limited to specific plowed routes serving Nordic ski hubs.

intel.title: Connectivity Gaps
intel.text: Cellular service is highly unreliable once you pass the Discovery Centres. Download offline maps and keep a physical copy of the Sépaq trail guide in your vehicle.

plan.arrival: Pick up your rental at YUL and drive north on Highway 15; stock up on local supplies in Saint-Jovite before checking into your sector-specific lodging.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are suitable for main park roads; verify rental terms for unpaved sector roads.
plan.goldenHour: La Corniche lookout offers the most dramatic light over the Laurentian valley at sunset, dependent on autumn haze.
